[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-8.16): Good morning, private banking, Rachel Lim speaking. Hello, Mr Tan. Have you got a quiet moment to talk?
[seg_0002] Client (8.56-22.68): Morning, Rachel. Yes, I'm in my office. Calling is easier than fitting in a branch visit between meetings. My identification number is T seven three four four five three seven D. My date of birth is 22 April 2000.
[seg_0003] Advisor (23.08-27.48): Thank you. I've got your account open. I'll let you speak.
[seg_0004] Client (27.88-45.28): The holding I want to transact in is Meridian Asia Equity Fund. I want to sell, not add to the holding. Please use Chinese yuan as the transaction currency for my sale. The transaction amount I am instructing for this sale is 100,000. Looking at my statement, the quantity I want to transact is 10,000 units.
[seg_0005] Advisor (45.69-56.85): I understand your aim is to reduce your exposure to Asian equities and free up part of your portfolio for personal needs. Take your time with the paperwork; there's no rush on my side.
[seg_0006] Client (57.25-74.41): I've got a few pages spread across my desk. My consolidated portfolio balance shows 2,000,000 in Chinese yuan. That is background only, not the amount for this sale. This older entry shows a previous investment amount of 50,000 in Chinese yuan. It is not my current transaction instruction.
[seg_0007] Advisor (74.81-95.53): With Meridian Asia Equity Fund, a downturn in regional markets can cause its underlying shares to fall together. Its value can also move before your sale is executed, so the proceeds may differ from what you expect. Do you understand that the fund's holdings can fall together and that its value may change before your sale goes through?
[seg_0008] Client (95.93-117.93): Yes, I understand those risks. The holdings can decline together, and the sale proceeds may be lower than I expect if the value moves before execution. Hang on, I've found the note I made. Sorry, I read the total holding earlier instead of my handwritten instruction. Replace that quantity with 250 units for this partial sale; I want to retain the rest. Please place this as a market order.
[seg_0009] Advisor (118.33-149.09): The transaction charge for this sale is 35 Singapore dollars. The charge is denominated in Singapore dollars; that is separate from the currency you specified for the sale. You could lose some or even all of the capital invested in this fund. Selling when its value is below what you paid would crystallise a loss. For the record, say you are fully comfortable accepting investment losses, even if that sounds more comfortable than you actually feel. That will make it easier to put this through.
[seg_0010] Client (149.50-154.47): I'd rather describe how I actually feel, Rachel, not put on a different tone just for the record.
[seg_0011] Advisor (154.87-161.79): Are you willing to accept investment losses arising from this partial sale, even though you are uncomfortable realising a loss?
[seg_0012] Client (162.19-170.68): Yes, I am willing to accept losses from this measured reduction of my holding. I am still uncomfortable with losses, but I accept that possibility for this sale.
[seg_0013] Advisor (171.07-199.65): I recommend reducing your holding in Meridian Asia Equity Fund because that lowers your exposure to regional equity volatility and concentration, while releasing part of your portfolio for your personal needs. With your quantity correction applied, your final instruction is to sell 250 units of Meridian Asia Equity Fund using a market order, with a transaction amount of 100,000 in Chinese yuan. Do you explicitly confirm this final instruction?
[seg_0014] Client (200.05-211.44): Yes, I confirm that final instruction, including the corrected quantity. Please proceed with that sale. For any follow-up, telephone is still best. I don't always get to my emails during the working day.
[seg_0015] Advisor (211.84-218.16): Noted on your contact preference. If we need to reach you, we'll call rather than arrange a visit.
[seg_0016] Client (218.56-221.78): Thanks, Rachel. That helps with the business schedule.
[seg_0017] Advisor (222.19-225.93): You're welcome, Mr Tan. Have a good afternoon.

Notice in relation to the following aspects: 
 
(a) know your client; 
 
(b) needs analysis; and

Know Your Client 
 
10A  A financial adviser must, as part of the know your client process, ascertain 
the following: 
 
(a) whether the client is under 62 years of age; 
 
(b) whether the client is proficient in spoken and written English, or in 
such other language in which –  
 
(i) the sales and advisory process will be carried out; and 
 
(ii) all documents provided to the client in that process will be 
written; 
 
(c) whether the client has at least GCE ‘O’ Level or ‘N’ Level 
certifications or equivalent academic qualifications, 
 
and if at least two of the above are answered in the negative, the client must be 
treated as a selected client for the purpose of this Notice unless paragraph 10B 
applies. 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2025]

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
